title: The Writer Who Invented Cyberpunk Has Never Played a Video Game
summary: William Gibson is one of the most important science fiction writers alive. His 1980s novel Neuromancer helped create cyberpunk, a whole genre of stories about hackers, high-tech cities, and virtual worlds. Video games have borrowed from his ideas for decades. There is just one funny detail: Gibson says he has never played a video game in his life. 'I've never played a video game in my life, but this thing [Grand Theft Auto] actually does [seem] interesting,' Gibson posted this weekend. He added that he was not saying he wanted to learn to play it, only that he found a clip of the new game intriguing in some mysterious way, in its 'texture' or 'depth.' Gibson built his imaginary worlds by watching real life. In the 1970s, he spent time around arcades in Vancouver, Canada, observing teenagers and the crowds around the machines, as computers changed from fridge-sized number crunchers into desktop workstations. From that, he invented the idea of 'cyberspace,' a word and a world that gamers and writers have used ever since. He may have tried Pong once, he told fans, 'on a tabletop in a bar?' But that is about it. Now Grand Theft Auto VI, the newest game from Rockstar, has pulled him in, at least as a viewer. Like thousands of others, Gibson has been watching viral clips of the game online. One clip that kicked off the conversation shows a boom barrier launching a character named Jason into the air like a catapult, much to the embarrassment of another character, Lucia. Other streamers have found their own strange corners of the game's world, called Leonida. One pretends to host a nature documentary while wandering the wilderness. Another features a dog driving a jetski to rescue Jason. 'I was enthralled by this one streamer pretending to host a nature documentary while wandering around the wilderness of Leonida,' wrote Defector's Brandy Jensen. 'I cheered as Jason is, for reasons that remain completely beyond me, rescued by a dog driving a jetski.' If the early sales figures are true, Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest-performing piece of media of all time. It has drawn in eager fans and curious onlookers alike, even a writer who helped invent the world it plays in and still has not picked up a controller.
why_it_matters: Gibson's ideas shaped the games millions of kids play, so it is funny and surprising that the man who imagined cyberspace has never played a game himself.

Grand Theft Auto is a hugely popular series of open-world games where players explore a big fictional city and its surrounding countryside.
